7Page | Öztimurlar UHRET

7Page, Öztimurlar MTAL UHRET topluluğu bünyesinde NASA Space Apps 2026'ya katılan genç geliştiricilerden oluşur. Yazılım, yapay zekâ ve uzay teknolojilerine odaklanıyoruz. 3D tasarım ve veri bilimine ilgi duyan ekip arkadaşları arıyoruz.

7Page represents the UHRET community at Öztimurlar Vocational High School. We focus on software, AI and space exploration, welcoming creative minds skilled in 3D design and data science.

Seven Pages. One Mission. Beyond Earth.
summary:
ARES Mission Control is an interactive Mars exploration planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms Martian terrain information into understandable, evidence-based route comparisons for future human surface missions.

Exploring Mars requires more than finding the shortest path. Astronauts must consider terrain elevation, slopes, travel distance, and uncertainty while reaching their scientific objectives.

Our application enables users to select exploration scenarios, examine alternative routes, visualize elevation profiles, and compare measurable route characteristics within a unified mission-planning interface. It combines interactive mapping with clear decision explanations, helping users understand the trade-offs between different paths.

ARES Mission Control emphasizes scientific transparency by distinguishing measured information from estimates and assumptions. Its bilingual English–Turkish interface also makes Mars exploration planning more accessible.

Our goal is to demonstrate how planetary science data can support safer, more informed exploration decisions and make complex Martian terrain understandable to a wider audience.
details:
ARES Mission Control

Evidence-Based Marswalk Route Planning

https://spcapps.openstacktool.com/

The Problem

Future human exploration of Mars will require careful planning across unfamiliar and potentially challenging terrain. Selecting an exploration route involves more than minimizing distance: elevation changes, terrain characteristics, scientific objectives, and uncertainty can all influence mission decisions.

Planetary observations contain valuable geographic information, but translating that information into practical route comparisons is not always straightforward.

Our Solution

ARES Mission Control is an interactive, browser-based mission-planning prototype designed to make Martian route analysis more understandable.

Users can explore predefined mission scenarios, examine alternative surface routes, and evaluate how their characteristics differ. The system presents quantitative information alongside visual explanations so that users can understand not only which route is preferable under a given set of assumptions, but also why.

Core Capabilities

1. Interactive Mission Planning

Users can select exploration scenarios and examine routes associated with specific mission objectives.

2. Alternative Route Comparison

The platform places alternative paths side by side, allowing users to compare their characteristics rather than automatically assuming that the shortest route is the best.

3. Terrain and Elevation Analysis

Elevation profiles help reveal changes in terrain along a planned traverse, adding geographic context to route evaluation.

4. Evidence-Based Decision Explanations

The interface connects route recommendations to measurable differences and explicitly avoids treating equal measurements as unequal.

5. Customizable Mission Workflows

Users can modify mission scenarios, with confirmation mechanisms designed to prevent accidental loss of existing planning work.

6. Accessible Bilingual Interface

English and Turkish controls help make the platform usable by a broader educational and technical audience.

Technical Approach

ARES Mission Control is implemented as an interactive web application. Its interface brings mission selection, route visualization, elevation analysis, and comparative decision information into a unified workflow.

Automated browser testing with Playwright is used to evaluate critical interactions, including mission restoration, route comparison, localization, and scenario replacement.

The project's design prioritizes understandable quantitative comparisons, consistent application behavior, and transparent presentation of uncertainty.

Innovation

The central innovation of ARES Mission Control is its decision-oriented approach to planetary mapping.

Rather than presenting Mars solely as a visual map, it enables users to investigate competing exploration routes and interpret the practical significance of their differences.

The system is designed to communicate evidence and trade-offs instead of presenting every calculated result as an unquestionable fact.

Intended Impact

ARES Mission Control demonstrates how planetary geographic information can be transformed into accessible mission-planning tools.

It can support educational demonstrations of Mars exploration, encourage scientific reasoning, and provide a foundation for future research into more sophisticated surface-navigation and decision-support systems.

Limitations and Future Development

ARES Mission Control is a prototype, not a flight-qualified navigation system.

Its results depend on the accuracy, resolution, coverage, and assumptions associated with the underlying data and calculations. The platform does not replace astronaut judgment, verified surface reconnaissance, or operational mission safety procedures.

Future development could expand data integration, terrain-hazard assessment, environmental constraints, and route-validation capabilities.
